title: Modi Marks Diwali in Bastar, Declares First Naxal-Free Festival
excerpt: At the CoBRA base in Karanpur, the Prime Minister told security personnel that every district is now free from Naxalism and that no CRPF jawan died on duty in the past year.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi spent Diwali on Sunday, November 8, 2026, with CoBRA personnel at the Karanpur operations base in Chhattisgarh's Bastar district.
  • Modi said this was the first Diwali when every district in the country was free from Naxalism, after what he described as victory in a decades-long war against Maoist terror.
  • He said no CRPF jawan had lost his life on duty in the past year, which he called the first such year in 47 years.
  • The visit was Modi's 13th consecutive Diwali with defence or security forces, and the first since the Centre declared the country free from Naxalism on March 31, 2026.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Diwali on Sunday with security personnel at the CoBRA Operations Base at Karanpur in Chhattisgarh's Bastar district, telling them India had won its decades-long war against Naxalism and that this was the first Diwali when every district of the country was free from it, according to IANS and ANI reports of the address.

The choice of venue carried the message. The Karanpur base served as a training centre and launchpad for counter-Naxal operations in Bastar and Abujhmad, areas once considered major strongholds of the Maoist insurgency, IANS reported. Modi said he had come to the forests of Bastar on behalf of 1.4 billion Indians to thank the personnel for their sacrifices.

"After 40-50 years, a Diwali like this has come. This is the first Diwali when the nation has won its decades-long war against Naxalism and Maoist terror. This is the first Diwali when every district of the country is free from Naxalism."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister

What Modi claimed in Bastar

Modi said crores of countrymen had overcome the fear of Naxalism, and credited security personnel for the outcome. "This is an incredible accomplishment, and a substantial amount of recognition should be attributed to you," he told the personnel, according to IANS.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfeO4nBpGgv/

He also pointed to a casualty milestone. "For the first time in 47 years, something remarkable happened: not a single CRPF jawan lost his life while on duty during the past year. This is a victory for the country's right policies and strong determination. This is a victory for your valour, courage and restraint," he said, according to ANI. The figures in the speech — the 47-year mark, the district counts and the comparisons with earlier years — were the Prime Minister's own statements in the address.

Modi told the personnel they were family to him, noting that millions of Indians were travelling home to celebrate the festival with their families.

The history he invoked

Modi contrasted the present with the years before his government took office. Between 2004 and 2013, he said, the number of security personnel martyred each year was higher than the number of Naxalites killed, and he alleged that governments of that time treated Naxalism as an "incurable disease" and left it unaddressed, ANI reported.

He recalled that more than 230 districts across nearly 20 states had once been affected by Left-Wing Extremism, with as many as 2,000 Naxal attacks in a single year, and that in 2010, in nearby Dantewada, 76 CRPF personnel were martyred in an encounter and 44 civilians killed in another incident the same year. Reports of the speech carried no response from the Congress.

He credited personnel from the CRPF, CoBRA, BSF, ITBP, SSB, IRB and state police forces, along with units such as the Bastar Fighters, and said development work in Naxal-affected areas had helped win public support for the forces.

Why Bastar, and why now

The visit followed the Centre's announcement on March 31, 2026, that the country had been freed from Naxalism, after several senior leaders and cadres were killed and hundreds of others surrendered, according to the reports. Bastar was long regarded as the epicentre of Maoist activity in Chhattisgarh. Modi said the region, once affected by Naxal terror, was now seeing a new phase of development because of the personnel's sacrifice and dedication.

The Bastar stop also continued a personal pattern. This was the 13th consecutive year Modi has spent Diwali with defence or security forces. Last year he marked the festival with naval personnel aboard INS Vikrant in Goa, and between 2014 and 2025 he visited soldiers on 12 occasions, with Jammu and Kashmir featuring most frequently, IANS reported.

What to watch

Modi framed internal security as the foundation of national strength. "When a nation's internal security is robust, external adversaries cannot succeed," he said. For diaspora readers with family in central India, the practical test will be whether Bastar and Abujhmad sustain normal civilian life and development work without a return of violence.
